## How the guide uses it

On 171 pages and the subject of pp. 5–15, where 20 contributors stake 62 priced positions. Each team page prints three futures markets. p. 38 carries an interview-driven piece in which a bookmaker discusses how playoff expansion tripled handle in national-championship and yes/no-playoff markets.

## Working definition — TTW DERIVED

A bet on a season-long outcome — a conference title, a playoff berth, a championship, an individual award — priced before or during the season.

## Why it matters — TTW DERIVED

It is the format most of the guide's opinion arrives in. Almost every argument the book makes eventually resolves into a futures price somebody is willing to take.

## How bettors use it in this guide

With explicit attention to price rather than to outcome alone. Contributors shop (Mitch Moss tells the reader the Ole Miss numbers are all over the map), size their stakes in printed units, and argue from relative pricing — Stormy Buonantony's New Mexico play rests entirely on two teams being level to win the conference while priced 10-1 and 20-1 to make the playoff.
